@l33tcy I've been thinking about this problem from a tangential perspective.   
  
I am tempted to build my own agent harness. Thing is semantic/vector search lacks directionality and representation of the 'how' of relevancy.   
  
Term search is good. What really has me curious is making a token efficient mechanism to manage context by compressing and decompressing intelligently as you build.   
  
Some things are obvious, like replacing a code change or diff with a line summary and file reference, but mapping out architectural concepts and viewing things at the right level of detail is... it's hard.

Report

Noctis Leonard [...] So on a big project, the agent never loads the codebase or the docs. It calls a tool, and gets back only the top few relevant chunks — reranked and capped to a fixed token budget. A 500-doc project and a 5-doc one send roughly the same amount to the model. The library grows, what hits the context doesn't.

Three things keep that slice sharp:

→ hybrid search (meaning + exact terms) so the right chunk wins, not just a nearby one

→ a hard token budget before anything reaches the prompt

→ memory that retires old facts when they change, so it doesn't slowly rot

Honestly the hard part isn't window size, it's retrieval quality. A clean 4k-token slice beats a stuffed 1M window on accuracy and cost. [...] Subscribe
